Quantified stake: At 4 t ha⁻¹ an APH2 crop removes 91 kg N ha⁻¹ in grain; the 25–50 kg N ha⁻¹ target covers 27–55% of it (Grain Trade Australia, 2025; Rogers & Oldroyd, 2014)
Position: Conditional; only if the grade stays reachable

Quantified stake: Grade is assigned on nitrogen × 5.7 at receival, so protein variability becomes blending and segregation cost (Grain Trade Australia, 2025)
Position: Resistant; bears a cost it does not cause

Quantified stake: HB4, the only approved transgenic wheat trait, is cleared in 10 countries but grown in 2 (ISAAA, 2025)
Position: Resistant; acceptance is separate from approval

Stakeholder: Smallholders on feed and domestic grades
Quantified stake: Fertiliser use in Africa averages about 22 kg ha⁻¹ against 94 in Latin America and 177 in Asia, and feed grades carry no protein floor (Food and Agriculture Organization [FAO], 2024; Grain Trade Australia, 2025)
Position: Strongest demand; the natural first market

Quantified stake: Bread wheat is a 17 Gb allohexaploid with 3 homoeologues per gene and 1.5–51% transformation efficiency (IWGSC, 2018; Debernardi et al., 2020)
Position: Cautious; wheat is the hardest cereal to engineer

Quantified stake: Wheat yields 1.2 t ha⁻¹ more after grain legumes and 0.5 t ha⁻¹ more after oats, so 0.7 t ha⁻¹ is the nitrogen component (Angus et al., 2015)
Position: Opposed; the trait substitutes for half their value

Quantified stake: Wheat straw has a C:N of 80–100:1 or higher, well above the 25:1 immobilisation threshold (García-Ruiz et al., 2019)
Position: Watchful; residue chemistry, not nitrogen, is their variable

Quantified stake: 185 Mt NH₃ produced annually, 98% from natural gas (Smith et al., 2020); wheat takes about 18% of manufactured reactive nitrogen (Ladha et al., 2016)
Position: Opposed; faces demand erosion, not a cost shock

Quantified stake: Inside wheat's 90–135 kg N ha⁻¹ window, substitution abates 0.91–1.08 times the constant-factor estimate (Shcherbak et al., 2014)
Position: Conditional on measurement; no premium for wheat
